evidence_excerpts: An initial control field Ω1(t1) produces entanglement between internal atomic states and the polarization state of a flying photon; a second control field Ω2(t2) returns the atom to its initial state while generating a second flying photon, thereby leading to entanglement between the two emitted fields.
text: Controlled cavity pulses can generate entanglement first between an atom and an emitted photon and then between sequentially emitted photon polarizations.
